coordinate_convention.reference_body: Moon (NAIF/Horizons ID 301, MEAN_ME pole/equator, R = 1737.4 km sphere)
coordinate_convention.longitude: East-positive degrees in [-180, 180] or [0, 360) (Horizons accepts both and normalises internally to [0, 360) East-positive)
coordinate_convention.altitude: Kilometres above lunar reference sphere (R = 1737.4 km)
coordinate_convention.notes: Verified against live JPL Horizons API response header: 'Center geodetic : E-lon(deg),Lat(deg),Alt(km)', 'Center pole/equ : MEAN_ME (high precision) {East-longitude positive}', 'Center radii : 1737.4, 1737.4, 1737.4 km'.

validation_sites.name: South Pole (reference point)

validation_sites.source_legacy: Approximate: IAU name centre of Shackleton crater, used as the pole reference, not a rim or landing site
validation_sites.notes: Validation-only south-polar reference point (-89.9 deg S). Not a public candidate landing site. Used to verify that solar elevation remains within ~1.5-1.65 deg of the horizon year-round.

validation_sites.notes: Validation-only far-side reference location. Not a public candidate landing site. Used to verify that Earth is never visible above the geometric horizon.
